Surah al-Rum (Surat al-Rum), Meccan except verse 17 which is Medinan, and its verses are sixty.

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by that.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 30, verse 2:

﴿The Romans have been defeated﴾. They are the People of the Book, but they were defeated by Persia, and the Persians are not People of the Book, rather they worship idols. So the disbelievers of Mecca rejoiced at that and said to the Muslims: "We will defeat you just as Persia defeated the Romans."

﴿In the nearest part of the land﴾, i.e., the nearest land of the Romans to Persia, in al-Jazirah (Upper Mesopotamia), where the two armies met; and the aggressor was the Persians. ﴿And they, after their defeat﴾, i.e., the Romans. The verbal noun is annexed to its object: i.e., the Persians' victory over them. ﴿Will overcome﴾ the Persians.

in bid'i sinin (fi bidʿi sinīn): it is what lies between three and nine, or ten, years. The two armies met in the seventh year from the first encounter, and the Romans defeated the Persians. "To Allah belongs the command, before and after" means: before the Romans' defeat and after it. The meaning is that the Persians' victory came first and the Romans' victory second, by the command of Allah, that is, His will. "And on that day" means the day the Romans are defeated.

With the victory of Allah, He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful. (Tafsir al-Jalalayn: the Byzantines rejoiced in the victory of Allah over the Persians, and they knew of it on the day it occurred, that is, the Day of Badr, by the descent of Jibril with the news of it, along with their joy in their own victory over the polytheists on that day.) ﴿He grants victory to whom He wills﴾ over the enemy, ﴿and He is the Almighty﴾ the Victorious, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ to the believers.

(Surah 30, verse 6)

﴿A promise of Allah⁠﴾ is a verbal substitute (maṣdar badal min al-lafẓ) for its verb; the original was "Allah promised them victory." ﴿Allah does not break His promise⁠﴾ with it. ﴿But most people⁠﴾ meaning the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿do not know⁠﴾ His promise to grant them victory.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 7:

﴿They know the outward appearance of the life of this world﴾, i.e., its livelihoods: trade, agriculture, building, planting, and other such things. ﴿And they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾. The repetition of "they" (hum) is for emphasis.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 8:

﴿Do they not reflect within themselves?﴾ So that they may turn back from their heedlessness. ﴿God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term.﴾ For this reason they will pass away when that term ends, and after it will be the resurrection. ﴿Indeed, many of the people﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿are, in the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.﴾ i.e., they do not believe in the resurrection after death.

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them?﴾ of the nations. It was their destruction because they denied their messengers. ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾ like ʿĀd and Thamūd. ﴿And they tilled the land﴾ they ploughed it and turned it over for sowing and planting. ﴿And they populated it more than these have populated it﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ with the manifest evidences. ﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them﴾ by destroying them without a crime. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ by denying their messengers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 30, verse 10:

﴿Then the final outcome of those who did evil was the worst (al-su'a), that they denied the signs of Allah﴾

"Al-su'a" is the feminine of "al-asw'a," meaning "the worst," "the most ugly." It is the predicate of "kana" (was), with "'aqibah" (outcome) in the nominative case as the subject... 

Let me correct that and give the faithful rendering of the passage as it stands:

The Arabic reads: "Ta'nith al-aswa'": al-aqbah, khabar kana 'ala raf' 'aqibah wa-ism kana 'ala nasb 'aqibah, wa-al-murad biha Jahannam wa-isa'atahum. Anna, ay: bi-an, kadhdhabu bi-ayat Allah, al-Qur'an.

Translation:

"Ta'nith al-asw'a" (the feminine form of al-asw'a): al-aqbah (the ugliest/worst). It is the predicate (khabar) of "kana" (was), with "'aqibah" in the nominative case (raf') as the predicate-related form, and the subject (ism) of "kana" in the accusative case (nasb) on "'aqibah." What is intended by it is Jahannam (Hell), and their evil deeds. "Anna" means "bi-an" (because/in that), i.e., that they "denied the signs of Allah," meaning the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 11:

﴿Allah originates creation﴾, i.e., He brings into being the creation of mankind; ﴿then He repeats it﴾, i.e., He creates them after their death; ﴿then to Him you will be returned﴾, with the ya' and the ta' (i.e., the verb may be read with yāʾ, "they will be returned," or with tāʾ, "you will be returned").
﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will despair﴾. The polytheists will fall silent, because their argument will be cut off.

﴿And there will not be﴾ i.e., there will not be ﴿for them, among their partners﴾, those whom they associated with Allah, and they are the idols, ﴿intercessors for them. And they will be﴾ i.e., they will become ﴿disbelievers in their partners﴾ i.e., disavowing them.
﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day﴾ is an emphasis (taʾkīd) ﴿they will be divided﴾: the believers and the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 15:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow﴾ (i.e., a garden) ﴿delighted﴾ (i.e., made joyful).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 16:

﴿And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾ (the Qur'an) ﴿and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ (the resurrection and what is other than it)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 17:

﴿So glorify Allah﴾, i.e., glorify Allah, meaning pray (ṣallū), ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, i.e., when you enter into the time of evening (masāʾ), and in it are two prayers: the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾, you enter into the time of morning (ṣabāḥ), and in it is the Ṣubḥ prayer.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 18:

﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth﴾ — an interjection (i'tiraḍ); its meaning: its inhabitants praise Him.

﴿And in the evening﴾ — coordinated with "ḥīn" (time); in it is the prayer of ʿAṣr (the afternoon prayer).

﴿And when you enter midday﴾ — you enter into the ẓahīrah (midday); in it is the prayer of Ẓuhr (the noon prayer).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 19:

﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾, like the human from the sperm-drop and the bird from the egg, ﴿and He brings the dead out of the living﴾, the sperm-drop and the egg from the living, ﴿and revives the earth﴾ with vegetation ﴿after its death﴾, i.e., its dryness, ﴿and thus﴾ the bringing forth ﴿you will be brought out﴾ from the graves, with the verb in the active and the passive voice (both readings).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 20:

﴿And among His signs﴾ (exalted is He), which indicate His power, ﴿is that He created you from dust﴾, i.e., your origin, Adam, ﴿then, behold, you are human beings﴾ of flesh and blood, ﴿dispersing﴾ throughout the earth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 21:

﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ So Hawwa' (Eve) was created from a rib of Adam, and the rest of mankind from the drops (nutfah) of men and women. ﴿That you may find tranquility in them﴾ and become familiar with them, ﴿and He placed between you﴾ all together ﴿affection and mercy. Indeed in that﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿are signs for a people who reflect﴾ upon the workmanship of God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 22:

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the variation of your tongues⁠ and colours﴾ i.e., your languages: Arabic, non-Arabic, and others, ﴿and your colours﴾ white, black, and other than these; and you are the children of one man and one woman. ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ indications of His power, Exalted is He, ﴿for those who know﴾ with the lām vowelled with a fatha or a kasra, i.e., those possessed of intellects and those endowed with knowledge.

{And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day} by His will, as rest for you; {and your seeking of His bounty} during the day, {by which He provides for you}, i.e., your moving about in seeking sustenance by His will. {Surely in that are signs for a people who hear} with contemplation and reflection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 24:

﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as a fear [for the traveler from the thunderbolts] and as a hope [for the resident for the rain]﴾ — that is, your being shown (ʾirāʾatikum, "the act of showing you") the lightning, ﴿as a fear﴾ for the traveler from the thunderbolts, ﴿and as a hope﴾ for the one who stays at home for the rain. ﴿And He sends down from the sky water, and by it He gives life to the earth after its death﴾ — that is, He spreads it out by causing it to grow [plants]. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ [which has been mentioned] ﴿are signs for a people who reflect﴾ — who contemplate.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 30, verse 25:**

﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command﴾, by His will, without pillars. ﴿Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth﴾, by having Israfil (the angel) blow into the Trumpet (ṣūr) for the Resurrection from the graves. ﴿Behold, you will come out﴾ from them, alive. So your coming out from them is by a call from His signs, exalted is He.
﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ in dominion, creation and servitude, ﴿all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ — obedient (muti'un).

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿And it is He who originates creation﴾ for the people ﴿then repeats it﴾ after their destruction ﴿and it is easier for Him﴾ than originating it, considering what is in the minds of those addressed, namely that repeating a thing is easier than beginning it; otherwise, for Allah, both are equal in ease ﴿And to Him belongs the highest likeness in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the highest attribute, which is that there is no god but Allah ﴿And He is the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His creation﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 30, verse 28:

﴿He has set forth⦅ḍaraba⦆ for you⦅laka-um⦆, O polytheists, a parable⦅mathalan⦆ from yourselves⦅min anfusikum⦆: Is there any of what your right hands possess⦅mimma malakat aymanukum⦆, i.e., of your slaves, who are partners⦅min shuraka'⦆ to you in what We have provided you⦅fi ma razaqnakum⦆ of wealth and other things, so that you and they are equal in it, and you fear them as you fear one another⦅takhafunahum kakhifatikum anfusakum⦆, i.e., as you fear your equals among the free? The interrogation carries the sense of negation. The meaning is: your slaves are not partners to you in what you possess, and so on. How, then, do you make some of God's slaves partners to Him?﴾ ﴿Thus⦅kadhalika⦆ We detail⦅nufassilu⦆ the signs⦅al-ayat⦆, that is, We make them clear in this same manner of detailing⦅mithla dhalika al-tafsil⦆ for a people who reflect⦅liqawmin ya'qiluna⦆, that is, who contemplate⦅yatadabbarun⦆.﴿

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 29:

﴿Rather, those who did wrong﴾ by associating partners with Allah ﴿followed their own desires without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has sent astray?﴾ That is, there is no guide for him. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ preventing them from the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 30:

﴿So set your face⁠ — O Muhammad⁠ — ﴿toward the religion⁠ ﴾ inclining to it, ﴿ḥanīfan﴾ (upright, inclining to it); that is, make your religion sincere to God, you and whoever follows you. ﴿The fiṭrah of God⁠﴾ — He created it ﴿upon which He created mankind⁠﴾, and it is His religion; that is, hold fast to it. ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of God⁠﴾ — in His religion; that is, do not alter it by associating partners with Him. ﴿That is the upright religion⁠﴾, the straight one, which is the Oneness of God. ﴿But most of mankind⁠﴾ — that is, the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿do not know⁠﴾ the Oneness of God.

﴿Munībīna﴾ (turning back in repentance) ﴿ilayhi﴾ (to Him, the Exalted), returning to Him in what He has commanded and forbidden. It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the subject of the imperative "aqim" (establish), and what is intended by it is: "Establish [your worship], [all of you]." ﴿Wattaqūhu﴾ (and fear Him): be mindful of Him, and fear Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 32:

﴿Of those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) by repetition of the preposition (al-jarr), ﴿split up their religion﴾ through their disagreement over what they worship, ﴿and became sects﴾ (shiya'an), divisions in that matter, ﴿each faction﴾ (hizb) of them ﴿rejoicing in what they have﴾ (ladayhim), that is, what is with them, ﴿exultant﴾, pleased with it. And in another reading, "fāraqū" (they abandoned), meaning: they left their religion which they had been commanded to follow.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 33:

﴿And when harm touches mankind﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿hardship﴾, i.e., severity, ﴿they call upon their Lord, turning back in repentance﴾, i.e., returning ﴿to Him﴾, not to any other, ﴿then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, by rain.

Here is the translation of the passage:

﴿So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them.﴾ It is intended as a threat. ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾ the outcome of your enjoyment. In it there is an iltifat (a shift in grammatical person) from the third person (ghaybah, absence) to the second person.

﴿Am﴾ (Or), in the sense of the interrogative hamza of denial (hamzat al-inkar) ﴿Have We sent down to them an authority﴾, meaning a proof, and a book, ﴿so that it speaks﴾, speaking by indication (dalalah), ﴿of what they used to associate with Him﴾, i.e., it commands them to associate partners with Him! No.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 36:

﴿And when We let the people taste mercy﴾ the disbelievers of Makkah and others ﴿mercy﴾ a blessing ﴿they rejoice in it﴾ a joy of insolence ﴿but if an evil﴾ a hardship ﴿befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ ﴿they despair﴾ they lose hope of mercy. It is the characteristic of the believer to give thanks at a blessing and to hope in his Lord at a hardship.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 37:

﴿Do they not see﴾ i.e., do they not know ﴿that Allah extends provision﴾ i.e., widens it ﴿for whom He wills﴾ as a test, ﴿and restricts it﴾ i.e., constricts it for whom He wills as a trial. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ in them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 38:

﴿So give to the near of kin his right﴾, [i.e., the kinship] (al-qaraba), [give him his due] of goodness (al-birr) and maintaining ties (al-silla), ﴿and to the needy and the wayfarer﴾, [i.e., the traveller] (al-musafir), [give] of charity (al-sadaqa). And the community (umma) of the Prophet follows him in this matter. ﴿That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah﴾, [i.e., His reward] for what they do, ﴿and it is those who are the successful﴾, [i.e., the ones who win].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 39:

﴿And whatever you give as riba﴾ — by way of a gift or present given to someone, so that one seeks more than it in exchange within the dealing; it is called by the name of what is sought, namely the increase (ziyadah) in the transaction. ﴿That it may increase within the wealth of people﴾ — of those who give — i.e., it may grow. ﴿Then it does not increase﴾ — it does not thrive (yazku) ﴿with Allah﴾; there is no reward in it for those who give. ﴿And whatever you give as zakah﴾ — charity (sadaqah) ﴿seeking﴾ thereby ﴿the Face of Allah — those are the ones who receive multiplied (al-mud'ifun)﴾ — their reward is multiplied for what they intended by it. There is a shift (iltifat) here from address (khitab) to third-person reference.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 40:

﴿Allah is the One Who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that?﴾ [Those] whom you associated with Allah. ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ [Exalted is He] above the partner [that] they associate with Him.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 30, verse 41:**

﴿Corruption has appeared on the land﴾, meaning the deserts (al-qifar), through the withholding of rain and the scarcity of vegetation, ﴿and the sea﴾, meaning the towns that lie along the rivers, through the scarcity of their water, ﴿because of what the hands of people have earned﴾, meaning because of sins. ﴿That He may let them taste﴾, with the verb read with the ya' (ي) and with the nun (ن), ﴿some of what they have done﴾, meaning its punishment, ﴿so that they may return﴾, meaning that they may repent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 42:

﴿Say﴾ to the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿Travel through the earth and look at how was the end of those before [you]. Most of them were polytheists﴾, so they were destroyed because of their polytheism, and their dwellings and homes were ruined (khawiyah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 43:

﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾ the religion of Islam ﴿before there comes a day that cannot be turned back from Allah﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection ﴿That Day they will be divided﴾ In it there is idgham (assimilation) of the taa' (ت) originally into the saad (ص): they will separate after the reckoning, into the Garden and the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 44:

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾ — its burden (wabal) of disbelief, which is the Fire. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾ — they make ready their dwellings in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 30, verse 45:

﴿That He may reward﴾ is related to "they will be separated" (yaṣṣaddaʿūn). ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ from His bounty; He will reward them. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾, meaning, He will punish them.

**And among His signs** (Exalted is He) **is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news**, meaning: to give you good news of the rain. **And that He may let you taste of His mercy** through them, which is the rain and the fertility. **And that the ships may sail** by them **by His command**, meaning by His will. **And that you may seek of His bounty**, meaning seek provision through trade on the sea. **Perhaps you will be grateful** for these blessings, O people of Makkah, so that you will affirm His oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 47:

﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs.﴾ [Clear proofs] with the evident arguments confirming their truthfulness in their message to them. ﴿So they denied them,﴾ [and] ﴿so We took retribution against those who committed crime.﴾ [We] destroyed those who denied them. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers.﴾ [Support] against the disbelievers by destroying them and saving the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 48:

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds, so they stir up a cloud﴾ drives it along, ﴿then He spreads it across the sky however He wills﴾ in terms of scattering and density, ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾ (the sin is read with a fatha or with a sukun), scattered pieces, ﴿and you see the rain﴾ (al-wadq, the rain) ﴿coming out from within it﴾ i.e., from its midst. ﴿Then when He causes it to fall upon whomever He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾ they are glad at the rain.

[And] indeed [they had been] before it was sent down to them, before it [the rain], "despairing" (ﷺ... no) — 

Here is the translation:

﴿And even though﴾ [qad, "indeed," is] an emphasis (ta'kid, reinforcement) ﴿they had been, before it was sent down to them, before it,﴾ ﴿utterly despairing﴾, meaning, despairing of its being sent down.

﴿So look at the traces﴾. In another reading, أثَر (athar, singular), ﴿of the mercy of Allah﴾, i.e., His bounty through the rain, ﴿how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, i.e., after its dryness, by causing it to grow plants.

﴿And if﴾ the *lām* here is the *lām al-qasam* (the lām of oath). ﴿We send forth a wind﴾ that is harmful to vegetation, ﴿and they see it [the crop] turn yellow, they would surely⦁ become﴾ *ṣārū* (they became), the answer of the oath, ﴿after it﴾ meaning after its yellowing, ﴿disbelievers﴾ *yakfurūn* (they deny), denying the blessing of the rain.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 30, verse 52:

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when﴾ [they turn their backs and leave]. Read with *tahqiq* (pronouncing both hamzas fully, without softening either; *tahqiq* means full articulation) for the two hamzas, and *tashil* (softening, a pronunciation between the hamza and the ya') for the second hamza, which sits between it and the ya'. The word discussed is ﴿أَءِذَا﴾ (*a-idha*), in which the second hamza is pronounced as a sound between hamza and ya'.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 53:

﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You cannot make anyone hear except those who believe in Our verses, so they are Muslims﴾ — ﴿you cannot make hear﴾ with the hearing of understanding and acceptance — ﴿except those who believe in Our verses﴾, the Qur'an — ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, sincere in the Tawhid (oneness) of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 54:

﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness﴾ (i.e., a despised fluid, water), ﴿then after weakness He made [you] strong﴾ (i.e., another weakness, which is the weakness of childhood), ﴿[then after] strength﴾ (i.e., the strength of youth), ﴿then after strength He made [you] weak again and gray-haired﴾ (i.e., the weakness of old age and the grayness of decrepitude). The word for "weakness" in all three instances may be pronounced with its first letter either vowelled with ḍammah (ḍu‘f) or fatḥah (ḍa‘f). ﴿He creates what He wills﴾ (of weakness, strength, youth and gray hair), ﴿and He is the All-Knowing﴾ (of the management of His creation), ﴿the All-Powerful﴾ (over whatever He wills).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 55:

﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾ — they will swear, [that is,] the disbelievers, ﴿that they had not remained [in the graves] except [for a short while]﴾ — in the graves. ﴿Thus were they deluded﴾ — they were turned away from the truth, namely the resurrection, just as they were turned away from the true statement about the duration of their stay [in the graves].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 56:

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith﴾ [say], from among the angels and others, ﴿"You have indeed remained, by the Decree of Allah, in what He wrote in His foreknowledge, until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection,"﴾ which you denied, ﴿but you did not know﴾ that it would occur.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 57:

﴿So on that Day the excuse of those who did wrong will not benefit them﴾ — read with the letter *yāʾ* (يَنْفَعُ, third person masculine) and with *tāʾ* (تَنْفَعُ, third person feminine), both readings being recited — ﴿their excuse﴾ in their denial of it ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ — it will not be required of them to seek *al-ʿutbā* (العُتْبَى), that is, to return to what pleases God.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 58:

﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾ — We made it; as a reminder to them. ﴿And if﴾ — the lam is a lam of oath — ﴿you bring them﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿a sign﴾ — like the staff and the hand given to Musa — ﴿they will surely say﴾ — the nun of the plural (nun al-raf') has been dropped due to the succession of nuns, and the waw is the plural pronoun, due to the meeting of two unvowelled letters — ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ among them — ﴿"You are not﴾ — i.e., Muhammad and his companions — ﴿but falsifiers﴾ — possessors of falsehoods."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 30, verse 59:

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾ the Tawhid (Oneness of God), just as He sealed the hearts of these people.

﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true, by His granting you victory over them,﴾ ﴿and let not those who have no certainty deter you﴾ concerning the Resurrection. That is: let them not move you to levity and haste by abandoning patience. That is: do not abandon it.
